description: มุน 2026-08-06 (M-D): the day-detail screen now reads goo's real DayDetail for all nine lower-half blocks, and the 8-gate 3×3 became a COMPASS driven by the data instead of by array order. The bug this guards SHIPPED: EightGates did `gates.map(...)` into a grid-cols-3 with the direction as a caption, so a cell's position was whatever order the pipe returned — it only looked right because the frozen content.ts array happened to match the order Figma drew. Opening Figma 634:8752 §12 and comparing it cell-by-cell against a real man-vs-day payload put every gate at the ANTIPODE of the pipe's — a clean 180° point reflection across all eight, between dates 23 days apart, because the gates rotate daily. Figma drew one day's fortune, not a layout; copying its positions freezes 14 July's reading forever, inverted, on a feature whose entire job is telling a user which way to go. No human review catches it: the direction caption travels inside the cell with the glyph, so the board reads correct by caption and wrong by position simultaneously. Fixed by REMOVING the freedom rather than watching it — position comes from one DIR_CELL table applied as explicit grid coordinates, so neither array order nor JSX order can move anything. scripts/gate-compass.test.ts asserts the table means what a COMPASS means (north up, east right, every opposite pair reflecting through the centre) rather than merely that the eight entries are distinct — the inverted table is also a perfect bijection, so a bijection check would have passed it. Teeth mut-compass-inverted (the shipped bug reproduced exactly) and mut-gate-dropped (an unreadable direction silently skipped), both verified biting. ⚠️ THE DOM LAYER IS STILL OPEN AND THIS ENTRY MUST NOT BE READ AS COVERAGE OF IT: ตู๋ demonstrated 2026-08-06 that deleting the two gridRow/gridColumn lines from EightGates.tsx makes the board wrong on 7 days in 8 while tsc, all 55 assertions here, every scripts test, and the capture log stay identical — because the test reads the TABLE and the component reads the TABLE, and nothing checks that the component still APPLIES it. 'The table is correct' and 'the board is correct' are different claims and only the second is what a user sees. The DOM and browser-geometry layers were deliberately not built (บอง 2026-08-06, a deadline call after ฟีม flagged 1.7× more harness than product), and the revisit condition in gate-compass.ts was ALSO wrong at first — it said 'if anyone touches this grid's CSS', which is the wrong door: the failure path is deleting a prop in the TSX and CSS never enters it. Corrected to: anyone editing EightGates.tsx's cell placement at all, or this grid's CSS, or a wrong-direction bug reaching a screen — and the DOM layer is the one to add first. Also decided and recorded as deliberate subtractions: no good/bad tint on gates (ตำราไม่มีเกณฑ์ — V2), dithi as plain text with no tone dots (V5), lucky colours set in DESIGN.md's existing per-element TEXT palette instead of Figma-sampled hexes (V1), advice on the main facet's card only (the pipe sends one list, not four). DayStrip's fake % / 干支 / tier tint were cut — they came from the fixture sine wave and sat directly above the real score ring, two numbers for one day on one screen. gate_layer=data-placement.
